service: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES), including NMES/FES for walking after spinal cord injury
vignette: 73-year-old woman with marked right quadriceps atrophy after 8 weeks in a long-leg cast for a tibial plateau fracture. Nerve conduction studies and EMG of the right lower limb are normal, showing intact peripheral nerve supply; she has no neurologic disease. Her physician prescribes a home NMES device to stimulate the resting quadriceps to treat the disuse atrophy.
rationale_note: Disuse atrophy from casting with intact nerve supply.

service: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES), including NMES/FES for walking after spinal cord injury
vignette: 66-year-old man with tibialis anterior and peroneal muscle atrophy 5 months after a traumatic laceration of the left common peroneal nerve at the fibular head. EMG shows complete denervation of the anterior and lateral compartment muscles with no voluntary motor units. His physician prescribes a home NMES device to treat the muscle atrophy.
rationale_note: Atrophy from denervation (nerve supply not intact), not disuse atrophy.

service: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES), including NMES/FES for walking after spinal cord injury
vignette: 70-year-old man with atrophy of the left forearm and hand muscles from disuse caused by contracture of burn scars over the left elbow and wrist, sustained 6 months ago. Nerve conduction studies show intact median, ulnar, and radial nerve function. He also has hypertension and type 2 diabetes without neuropathy. His physician prescribes an NMES device to treat the disuse atrophy.
rationale_note: Disuse atrophy from burn scar contracture is one of the NCD's listed examples; nerves intact.

service: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES), including NMES/FES for walking after spinal cord injury
vignette: 54-year-old man on Medicare through disability with a complete T10 spinal cord injury from a fall 2 years ago, including spinal stabilization surgery 2 years ago; neurologically stable since. Lower motor units L1 and below are intact on EMG and nerve conduction testing. He shows brisk muscle contractions to NMES with adequate sensory perception, transfers independently, stands independently in a frame for 5 minutes, has normal hand function to work the controls, has stable joints and upper and lower extremity strength to hold an upright posture, and has no hip or knee degenerative disease, osteoporotic fractures, pacemaker, severe scoliosis or osteoporosis, skin disease or cancer at the stimulation sites, irreversible contracture, or autonomic dysreflexia. He is highly motivated and committed to long-term use. Over the past 3 months he completed exactly 32 sessions of one-on-one training with the FES device, each performed directly by a physical therapist in an outpatient hospital department, aimed at walking. His physician orders an FES device for walking.
rationale_note: Boundary: exactly 32 one-on-one PT sessions over 3 months; all FES characteristics met.

service: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES), including NMES/FES for walking after spinal cord injury
vignette: 48-year-old woman on Medicare through disability with an incomplete T8 spinal cord injury 3 years ago; she has had no surgery for over 2 years. Lower motor units L1 and below are intact. She has brisk muscle contractions to NMES with sufficient sensory perception, transfers independently, stands independently for 4 minutes, has full hand function, stable joints, and no hip or knee degenerative disease, osteoporotic fracture, pacemaker, severe scoliosis or osteoporosis, skin lesions at stimulation sites, contracture, or autonomic dysreflexia. rationale_note: Only 24 training sessions completed; at least 32 are required.

service: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES), including NMES/FES for walking after spinal cord injury

service: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES), including NMES/FES for walking after spinal cord injury

service: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES), including NMES/FES for walking after spinal cord injury

service: Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES), including NMES/FES for walking after spinal cord injury
